title: Cross-host Linux and macOS effect evidence
description: Objective: collect production-surface effect conformance evidence on actual Linux and macOS hosts for every frozen platform boundary, bound to one exact source commit and distribution. Deliverable: host-native fault schedules/evidence receipts and a reproducible cross-host aggregation protocol. NOT in scope: implementing platform classifiers, running off-host fixtures as proof, or weakening Windows behavior. Hard dependencies: Linux boundary task-f01ef545b1554a2cb5df340ce78f6a5c, macOS boundary task-45d12ecfa6ae4938b23af28fe7876a44, doctor task-1cafc7f9fcdc4c9299860b6b1e38275d, and distribution packaging task-739879d0d1ce4a7ea4d1430688cdc4dc. Measured at HEAD 30458af on win32: tests/fault/linux/** and tests/fault/macos/** are absent; archived tasks-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275/e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856 have no landing commits, and their reopen notes explicitly require live Linux/macOS hosts. Consumer: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93. Owned paths: tests/fault/linux/**, tests/fault/macos/**, cross-host evidence manifests/aggregation, and CI/host runner configuration only where approved.
definitionOfDone: On an actual Linux host and an actual macOS host, every hand-written PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES member runs crash-before/after activation and cancellation schedules against the production classifier/runner surface; each schedule asserts exact PROVEN/UNKNOWN code, layer, boundary, and a nonzero case count.

Each host record binds source commit, distribution manifest/digest, OS/kernel/arch, Node/pnpm/provider runtime closure, fixture/fault schedule digests, timestamps, and raw run receipts; unverifiable or mismatched bindings yield UNKNOWN and never PASS.
Linux and macOS receipts are canonical, immutable, independently verifiable, and aggregated without trusting caller-selected host claims; missing host evidence leaves only that OS row UNKNOWN.
No off-host test fixture, emulation label, or design claim is accepted as host proof; Windows stays a separate observation and is not weakened.
Host-native fault gates and the cross-host verifier exit 0, and task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 is recorded as the acceptance consumer.
taskRails: This task requires real Linux and macOS execution environments; do not claim completion from win32 alone.
Use production @moe/runner/platform and distribution/doctor surfaces, not test reimplementations.
Every refusal/unknown asserts stable code plus layer/boundary and every generated schedule asserts positive cardinality.

implementationPlan.description: Start RED with hostile contract/aggregation tests and two hand-written host suites. In the cross-host fault test, specify exact-key immutable receipt/aggregate versions, canonical bytes and self-digest rules, fixed expected host slots (`linux`, `darwin`), and frozen failure layers `CROSS_HOST_COLLECTOR` / `CROSS_HOST_AGGREGATOR` with exact codes `CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_MALFORMED`, `CROSS_HOST_HOST_UNVERIFIABLE`, `CROSS_HOST_HOST_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_SOURCE_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_RUNTIME_UNVERIFIABLE`, `CROSS_HOST_SCHEDULE_INCOMPLETE`, `CROSS_HOST_SCHEDULE_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_RAW_RECEIPT_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_MISSING`, and `CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_DUPLICATE`. Generate tamper cases for every binding, assert the generated count is positive, and assert exact code, layer, host slot, and `UNKNOWN` rather than only failure. In each OS suite, independently hand-name the production seven-boundary tuple and three schedules (`CRASH_BEFORE_ACTIVATION`, `CRASH_AFTER_ACTIVATION`, `CANCELLATION`), assert the 7x3 product is exactly 21 unique cases, and make the matching-host path fail until the real driver exists; a wrong host must assert `CROSS_HOST_HOST_MISMATCH` at `CROSS_HOST_COLLECTOR`, emit no PROVEN receipt, and never be skipped as proof.
implementationPlan.note: RED first, observed. Wrote tests/fault/cross-host/effect-evidence.fault.ts plus the two hand-written OS suites before any protocol code existed; `pnpm exec tsc -p tests/fault/tsconfig.json` failed with TS2307 on ./effect-evidence-contract.js and ./effect-schedule-driver.js, which is the RED for this step. The hostile suite pins the exact-key receipt/aggregate versions, canonical sorted-key bytes, the fixed slots ["linux","darwin"], both frozen layers, and all 12 exact codes as a 12-member unique tuple. The tamper sweep generates 14 mutations (extra key, missing key, host spoof, doctor arch, kernel release, wrong source commit, one manifest digest, one asset digest, runtime truthClass, runtime pinningMethod, schedule universe, one raw case, schedule digest, self digest), asserts the generated count is positive AND exactly 14, and asserts exact code + exact layer + exact host slot per case rather than only that it failed. Thirteen of the fourteen are RE-SEALED through the production sealing function before verification, so each is the forgery an attacker would actually present and not merely a broken checksum; only the self-digest case is left unsealed. Aggregation cases pin PROVEN/PROVEN, missing-slot, duplicate-slot and cross-filed-slot behaviour and assert the other slot's valid row survives. Each OS suite hand-names the seven boundaries and three schedules independently, asserts them against the imported production PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES and CROSS_HOST_SCHEDULES, and asserts the 7x3 product is exactly 21 unique cases; the off-host branch is a real assertion (CROSS_HOST_HOST_MISMATCH at CROSS_HOST_COLLECTOR, no receipt) and never `it.skip`.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the typed evidence protocol, not a replacement platform classifier. Provide sorted-key UTF-8 canonical encoding, SHA-256 projection/digest helpers, total exact-key decoders, deep-frozen accepted values, content-addressed receipt/aggregate filenames, `verifyHostReceipt(expectedSlot, bytes, expectedSourceAndDistribution)`, and an aggregator over the fixed Linux/darwin slots. A receipt must bind Git source SHA/object format; all six canonical distribution components with manifest and asset digests plus a common aggregate digest; production doctor OS/arch/Node/pnpm report and its digest; kernel; production provider runtime observation/closure and digest; schedule/fixture/config/workflow/lockfile digests; canonical timestamps; exactly 21 raw case records and their digests; receipt version/digest; and consumer `task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93`. Verification must recompute every digest and derive the row from verified doctor/runtime identity rather than a caller host claim or artifact name. A missing, malformed, duplicate, stale-source, distribution-divergent, runtime-unverifiable, incomplete, or tampered input yields a frozen UNKNOWN row with the exact code/layer; one bad or absent slot must not erase the other slot's valid row.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN for the protocol: the 7 non-CLI cases of cross-host/effect-evidence.fault.ts now pass (3 CLI cases stay red until step 5). effect-evidence-contract.ts holds vocabulary and canonical encoding only: sorted-key recursive UTF-8 canonical JSON, sha256Hex/canonicalDigest, frozen slots/layers/12 codes, exact-key decoder, sealHostReceipt, and content-addressed receipt-<digest>.json. effect-evidence-verify.ts holds verification and aggregation. PLAN DEVIATION, deliberate and per-file-cap driven: the plan named verifyHostReceipt inside effect-evidence-contract.ts, but a single module would have exceeded the 250-line per-file cap (contract is 196 physical lines, verify is 253 - see step 7 for the split I still owe on verify). Splitting them also keeps the contract free of any import cycle, since verify imports contract and never the reverse. Bindings a receipt carries, all exact-key: source {commitSha, objectFormat}; distribution {componentCount, components[{name, manifestDigest, assetDigest}], aggregateDigest}; doctor {os, arch, nodeVersion, pnpmVersion, reportDigest}; kernel {release}; runtime {closureKind, pinningMethod, observationDigest, truthClass}; schedule {scheduleDigest, fixtureDigest, configDigest, workflowDigest, lockfileDigest}; timestamps {startedAt, completedAt}; 21 cases; caseDigest; receiptVersion; hostSlot; consumerTaskId task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93; plus the self receiptDigest. Gate order is load-bearing: shape, then self-digest recompute, then doctor/kernel identity, then derived-slot equality, then source, then distribution, then runtime, then the raw schedule. The row is DERIVED from the verified doctor.os inside the digest-checked bytes and must equal both the requested slot and the receipt's own hostSlot - a caller hostSlot field, a file name or a download directory never decides it. scheduleDigest covers only the case UNIVERSE (boundary/schedule pairs) while caseDigest covers the full case records, so tampering one case record is CROSS_HOST_RAW_RECEIPT_MISMATCH and cannot hide behind the schedule digest. Aggregation verifies each fixed slot independently: 0 receipts is CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_MISSING, >1 is CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_DUPLICATE, and a bad or absent slot leaves the other slot's PROVEN row standing; aggregate truth is AND over a length-checked row set so a truncated row list cannot read as PROVEN.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the shared real-host schedule driver using only Node built-ins and public package roots. Derive the executing host from `collectDoctorVersionReport()` plus `os.release()`, never a matrix/env claim. For each unique case, create unique effect/grant/process identities (the verifier registry is process-global), use production activation, and invoke the OS child launcher only after ACTIVATED. Before-activation schedules tombstone first, assert zero physical launch plus `EFFECT_TOMBSTONED` / `ACTIVATION` / `detail.leg=tombstoneWitness`, then classify an absent fact as `UNKNOWN` with `PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT`, the exact OS layer, and exact boundary. After-activation crash schedules wait for a real `process.execPath` verifier child to start, SIGKILL and observe it, assert `VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXIT_AMBIGUOUS` / `CAPTURE` / source `PROCESS`, and feed production `classifyCrash`; cancellation schedules start the real child, request ACTIVE cancellation (`MUST_DRAIN`), abort/observe it, assert `VERIFIER_PROCESS_CANCELLED` / `CAPTURE` / source `PROCESS`, and feed production `reconcileClaudeRun`. Build each boundary fact through its owner: runtime observation from the actual Node executable bytes/closure, scope plus input manifest with at least one tracked path, a real temp symlink/lstat/realpath observation, activation commit lease binding, reconciliation, and crash classification. Invoke the appropriate production boundary classifier for every case and the production whole-platform observer for every seven-case schedule batch; record exact truth/code/layer/boundary and raw process/timing/digest facts. Use bounded waits and `finally` cleanup so no child or temp path survives.
implementationPlan.note: Real-host schedule driver landed, Node built-ins plus the two bare package roots only. Executing host derives from collectDoctorVersionReport().observed.platform plus os.release(); a slot that does not equal the measured OS returns CROSS_HOST_HOST_MISMATCH at CROSS_HOST_COLLECTOR before any effect. Per-case identities are `${process.pid}-${counter}` because the verifier run registry is process-global and one-use. CRASH_BEFORE_ACTIVATION runs production applyEffectTombstone, then activateEffect with the tombstone, and requires exactly EFFECT_TOMBSTONED + layer ACTIVATION + detail.leg=tombstoneWitness; the launcher is never reached so tombstonedLaunchCount is a MEASURED zero, and every boundary fact is null, which the OS classifier answers UNKNOWN/PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT at the exact OS layer. CRASH_AFTER_ACTIVATION spawns a real process.execPath child that writes to stdout and SIGKILLs itself; CANCELLATION spawns a real long-lived child and aborts an AbortSignal 250ms after the launcher reported its pid. Both require source PROCESS and refuse the run if runVerifierProcess returns ok or a foreign refusal. VERIFIED LOCALLY BY DRILL (throwaway probe created, run, deleted in the same command; nothing tracked): tombstone -> EFFECT_TOMBSTONED/ACTIVATION with launches=0; cancellation -> VERIFIER_PROCESS_CANCELLED/CAPTURE with a real pid; runtime observation -> PROVEN/CONTENT_ADDRESSED_COPY from the actual node executable bytes. The drill also found and fixed two real defects: classifyCrash returned REFUSED/RECOVERY_OWNERSHIP_TRANSFER_UNPROVEN because adoption needs a real fence advance, so the record set now carries an advancedAuthority proof with epoch+1 AND a newly minted token (production then answers ADOPTED/ok); and pathFact threw EPERM on a filesystem that refuses symlinks, so it now fails closed to null and removes its temp tree in finally. Post-fix drill on this win32 host classified PROVIDER_LAUNCH, GIT_WORKSPACE, LOCK, SIGNAL_CANCELLATION, RUNTIME_CLOSURE and CRASH_RECOVERY as PROVEN and only PATH_SYMLINK as UNKNOWN/PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT (Windows symlink EPERM plus the POSIX absolute-path rule) - that is a debugging measurement on win32 and is NOT offered as host proof for either row. Every case invokes the per-boundary classifier AND the whole-platform observer for its seven-case batch, and a disagreement between them refuses rather than picking one. PLAN DEVIATION: the driver was 397 physical lines, so activation/child-process work moved into effect-schedule-activation.ts; driver is now 222 and activation 200, both inside the per-file cap.

implementationPlan.description: Finish the thin Linux/macOS suites and add the Node 24 collector/aggregator CLI. The Linux file must pin `linux`/`PLATFORM_LINUX`; the macOS file must pin `darwin`/`PLATFORM_MACOS`; on-host they run all 21 cases, assert the exact runner and platform outcomes, positive launch/case counts, and write only raw schedule evidence to a bounded requested directory. The `.mjs` CLI must call the real `buildReleaseSubject` (kept out of the TS import graph because `tsc -p tests/fault/tsconfig.json` otherwise raises TS7016), generate an ephemeral Ed25519 verification key, and retain only source-bound unsigned manifest/asset digests for cross-host identity—never compare key-dependent container/signature digests. Its `collect` mode combines an on-host raw schedule with fresh Git/release/doctor/runtime/file measurements and writes a content-addressed canonical receipt; its `aggregate` mode rebuilds the expected source/distribution from the checked-out commit, reads the two fixed slot directories, verifies both independently, always writes a canonical aggregate, and exits nonzero under `--require-complete` unless both rows are PROVEN. Invalid CLI/input paths must return a structured exact CROSS_HOST code/layer, not throw. Exercise both CLI modes from the fault test with temp directories; fixture-generated outputs are integrity tests only and are never labeled host proof.
implementationPlan.note: Both OS suites and the collector/aggregator CLI landed; `pnpm test:fault` is EXIT=0 with Test Files 7 passed (7) and Tests 61 passed (61), up from the 4/47 merge-base baseline. Linux pins slot "linux" and layer PLATFORM_LINUX; macOS pins "darwin" and PLATFORM_MACOS. On-host each runs all 21 cases and asserts, per case, UNKNOWN + PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT + the exact OS layer + a null pid for CRASH_BEFORE_ACTIVATION and PROVEN + null code + null layer + a positive pid for the two post-activation schedules, plus launchCount > 0, tombstonedLaunchCount === 0 and an inspected-count assertion of exactly 21 so a zero-case sweep cannot pass. Raw evidence goes only to MOE_CROSS_HOST_RAW when the caller sets it, and writeRawSchedule always prints executedCaseCount=<n> so a CI leg that exits 0 having run nothing is visible. CLI is Node 24 .mjs, outside the TS graph, calling the real buildReleaseSubject with a freshly generated ephemeral Ed25519 key. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: building the subject twice with two different ephemeral keys showed manifestDigest and containerDigest are key-DEPENDENT while assetDigests are stable, and componentCount is 6 (daemon, control-room, mcp-bridge, provider-claude, provider-codex, ide-adapter-jetbrains). The receipt therefore retains only key-independent source-bound digests: assetDigest = canonicalDigest(assetDigests) and manifestDigest = canonicalDigest of the unsigned source-bound manifest projection (componentId, componentKind, assetDigests, sourceSha). No container or signature digest is ever compared. collect refuses with an exact code and layer rather than throwing: unknown slot and host/schedule disagreement are CROSS_HOST_HOST_MISMATCH at CROSS_HOST_COLLECTOR, an unreadable or non-21-case schedule is CROSS_HOST_SCHEDULE_INCOMPLETE, an unpinned runtime is CROSS_HOST_RUNTIME_UNVERIFIABLE, and a distribution that will not rebuild is CROSS_HOST_DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH. aggregate rebuilds source and distribution from the checked-out commit (or --expect for the fixture test), reads both fixed slot directories, verifies each independently, ALWAYS writes the canonical aggregate, and exits 1 under --require-complete when truthClass is not PROVEN. Three fault cases drive the CLI end to end with temp directories; all CLI-generated output in those cases is an integrity fixture and is never labelled host proof. PLAN DEVIATION: plain Node does not map a .js specifier onto a .ts file (measured: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on effect-evidence-contract.js), so two one-line .js bridges were added next to the TS modules, exactly the convention packages/runner/src already uses (`export * from "./x.ts";`). Without them the CLI cannot import the protocol and would have to re-implement it.

implementationPlan.description: Extend (do not weaken or replace) the existing cross-host workflow with an independent `host-evidence` include-matrix whose exact job names are `host-evidence-linux` on `ubuntu-latest` and `host-evidence-darwin` on `macos-latest`, plus `cross-host-aggregate`. Keep pinned Node 24.16.0/pnpm 11.0.8, frozen install, `permissions: contents: read`, fail-fast false, and the existing broad gate unchanged so foreign baseline red remains visible. Each host job compiles the fault tree, runs only its matching fault file under the serial fault Vitest config, captures the real Vitest status through `PIPESTATUS[0]`, requires nonzero `Test Files` and `Tests` lines and the internal `executedCaseCount=21`, runs collector mode, and uploads `cross-host-{linux|darwin}-${{ github.sha }}` with upload-artifact v4 and `if-no-files-found:error`. The aggregate job depends only on the evidence matrix and uses `if: always()`: checkout the same SHA, download each artifact into its fixed expectation slot (transport names confer no authority), run the focused hostile contract test with nonzero counts, run aggregate mode `--require-complete`, and upload `cross-host-aggregate-${{ github.sha }}` even on refusal. No Windows source/test/workflow behavior is changed, and no off-host fixture or matrix variable can produce PROVEN.
implementationPlan.note: Workflow EXTENDED, never weakened: the existing `gate` job (ubuntu-latest + macos-latest, fail-fast false, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test) is byte-identical - the diff is pure append. Its foreign baseline red therefore stays visible instead of being deleted to buy a green run. Added `host-evidence` with an include-matrix producing exactly the API job names `host-evidence-linux` (ubuntu-latest) and `host-evidence-darwin` (macos-latest), plus `cross-host-aggregate`. Both new jobs pin pnpm 11.0.8 and Node 24.16.0, install --frozen-lockfile, declare `permissions: contents: read` per job (kept off the workflow root so `gate` behaviour is untouched), and the matrix sets fail-fast: false so a red Linux leg cannot cancel macOS. Each host job compiles the fault tree, runs ONLY its matching OS fault file under the serial fault Vitest config, and reads the real Vitest status out of ${PIPESTATUS[0]} because a `| tee` pipeline otherwise reports tee's status. Exit 0 alone is not accepted: the leg additionally requires a nonzero `Test Files N passed` line, a nonzero `Tests N passed` line, and the literal `executedCaseCount=21`. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: a throwaway probe (created, run, deleted in one command) confirmed Vitest forwards a worker `process.stdout.write` verbatim to the piped log, and the same probe with a broken file printed `Test Files 1 failed` / `Tests no tests`, which is exactly the vacuous shape these greps exist to catch. Receipts upload as cross-host-linux-${{ github.sha }} / cross-host-darwin-${{ github.sha }} with upload-artifact v4 and if-no-files-found: error. cross-host-aggregate needs only [host-evidence] and runs `if: always()`, checks out ${{ github.sha }}, downloads each artifact with continue-on-error into a FIXED slot directory (a missing artifact leaves that slot empty rather than failing the job), runs the focused hostile contract suite with the same nonzero-count and PIPESTATUS discipline, runs aggregate mode --require-complete, and uploads cross-host-aggregate-${{ github.sha }} with `if: always()` so a refusal still publishes evidence. The transport name confers no authority - the aggregator re-derives each row from the verified doctor identity inside the receipt, so a receipt filed into the wrong slot is CROSS_HOST_HOST_MISMATCH. No Windows source, test or workflow behaviour changed.

planningNotes.risks: Real completion has an external handoff: gh is not installed and repository policy forbids worker push, so an authorized human/governor must publish the exact committed SHA; an older run cannot satisfy the task. Shared-tree HEAD can move, so the run SHA, committed owned bytes, receipts, and verification query must all be rechecked after publication. Preserve the existing broad job even if it is foreign-red; the exact gate requires only the three evidence jobs and discloses every other red via path-attributed baseline. Use unique verifier identities because its registry is module-global; wait for observed STARTED/PID before SIGKILL/abort, bound every wait, and clean children/temp dirs in finally. macOS `/var` may realpath to `/private/var`, so bind observed path/target bytes rather than textual assumptions. Compare unsigned manifest/asset digests, not ephemeral-key container bytes. The MJS-to-TS direction relies on the pinned Node 24 erasable-TypeScript loader; TS must never import the untyped MJS. Wrong-host execution must remain UNKNOWN and must not emit a proof receipt.
